meta.framework: HIPAA Security Rule — 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C
meta.note: All controls are synthetic/sample data. No real PHI or production system data.

controls.title: Security Management Process — Risk Analysis
controls.description: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity.
controls.assessment_question: Has the entity conducted a documented risk analysis within the last 12 months covering all ePHI systems?
controls.evidence_type: Risk analysis report, asset inventory, system diagram

controls.title: Security Management Process — Risk Management
controls.description: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
controls.assessment_question: Does the entity maintain a risk management plan with documented mitigation strategies for identified risks?
controls.evidence_type: Risk management plan, POAM, mitigation evidence
common_failures: Residual risk not accepted by management

controls.title: Sanction Policy
controls.description: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented and enforced sanction policy for security policy violations, including ePHI breaches?
controls.evidence_type: HR policy, documented enforcement cases
common_failures: Violations not tied to security training

controls.title: Information System Activity Review
controls.description: Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
controls.assessment_question: Are audit logs reviewed regularly (at least monthly) with documented findings and follow-up actions?
controls.evidence_type: Audit review logs, SIEM dashboards, incident tickets
common_failures: No assignment of findings to owners

controls.title: Assigned Security Responsibility
controls.description: Identify the security official who is responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by this subpart.
controls.assessment_question: Is a Security Officer (or Privacy/Security Officer) formally designated with documented responsibilities?
controls.evidence_type: Job description, org chart, appointment memo
common_failures: Title exists but no time allocated

controls.title: Workforce Security — Authorization and Supervision
controls.description: Implement procedures for the authorization and supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information.
controls.assessment_question: Are workforce members' ePHI access rights authorized by management and reviewed at termination/role change?
controls.evidence_type: Access request forms, manager approval records, termination checklists

controls.title: Workforce Security — Clearance Procedure
controls.description: Implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to electronic protected health information is appropriate.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented clearance/background check process for employees with ePHI access?
controls.evidence_type: Background check policy, HR records
common_failures: No background checks for ePHI roles

controls.title: Workforce Security — Termination Procedure
controls.description: Implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when the employment of, or other arrangement with, a workforce member ends.
controls.assessment_question: Are access termination procedures executed within 24 hours of workforce member departure?
controls.evidence_type: Termination checklists, IT deprovisioning logs, account audits

controls.title: Information Access Management — Access Authorization
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures for granting access to electronic protected health information based on user role and need-to-know.
controls.assessment_question: Is role-based access control (RBAC) implemented with documented role definitions and periodic access recertification?
controls.evidence_type: Role matrix, access recertification records, IAM policy
common_failures: Role definitions not aligned to job functions

controls.title: Information Access Management — Access Establishment/Modification
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures that establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.
controls.assessment_question: Are all access grants and modifications documented with business justification and manager approval?
controls.evidence_type: Access request tickets, change logs, approval chains

controls.title: Information Access Management — Access Revocation
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures to terminate access when no longer needed (includes emergency access).
controls.assessment_question: Is emergency/temporary access automatically revoked after a defined timeframe with post-use review?
controls.evidence_type: Emergency access policy, automated revocation logs, review records

controls.title: Information Access Management — Minimum Necessary
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures that restrict access to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.
controls.assessment_question: Are access controls configured to enforce minimum necessary principle (e.g., field-level restrictions, segmented databases)?
controls.evidence_type: Data segmentation design, access control matrices, DB permissions
common_failures: All users see all patient records
Reports dump full tables without filtering

controls.title: Security Awareness and Training
controls.description: Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of its workforce (including management).
controls.assessment_question: Is annual security awareness training mandatory, tracked, and role-based (pharmacy tech vs admin vs IT)?
controls.evidence_type: Training records, completion reports, curriculum outline
common_failures: Training not completed by all staff

controls.title: Security Awareness — Protection from Malicious Software
controls.description: Procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.
controls.assessment_question: Are endpoints protected with anti-malware/EDR, with real-time scanning and centralized alerting?
controls.evidence_type: EDR console, AV policy, incident response records

controls.title: Security Awareness — Password Management
controls.description: Procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.
controls.assessment_question: Are password policies enforced (length, complexity, rotation, MFA) across all ePHI systems?
controls.evidence_type: AD/IdP policy, password audit results, MFA enrollment stats

controls.title: Security Awareness — Log-in Monitoring
controls.description: Procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
controls.assessment_question: Are failed logins, off-hours access, and anomalous location logins monitored and alerted?
controls.evidence_type: SIEM rules, login monitoring dashboard, alert tickets
common_failures: False positive rate too high (alert fatigue)

controls.title: Security Awareness — Contingency Operations
controls.description: Procedures for reporting and responding to security incidents during contingency operations (e.g., system failure, breach during recovery).
controls.assessment_question: Does the contingency plan include security-specific procedures (e.g., backup integrity checks, alternative site hardening)?
controls.evidence_type: DR plan, backup verification logs, alternative site assessment

controls.title: Security Incident Procedures
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents, including detection, response, and mitigation.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented incident response plan with defined roles, escalation paths, and OCR reporting timelines?
controls.evidence_type: IR plan, incident tickets, tabletop exercise records
common_failures: No distinction between security incident and breach

controls.title: Security Incident — Response and Reporting
controls.description: Identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate harmful effects; document and report.
controls.assessment_question: Are all security incidents documented with timeline, impact assessment, and lessons learned?
controls.evidence_type: Incident tickets, post-mortem reports, OCR notification records
common_failures: Breach threshold not calculated (500+ individuals trigger OCR)

controls.title: Contingency Plan — Data Backup Plan
controls.description: Establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information.
controls.assessment_question: Are ePHI backups encrypted, tested for restorability at least annually, and stored offsite/with redundancy?
controls.evidence_type: Backup logs, restore test results, encryption certificates
common_failures: Single point of failure (one backup target)

controls.title: Contingency Plan — Disaster Recovery Plan
controls.description: Establish and implement procedures to restore any loss of data.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented disaster recovery plan with RTO/RPO targets, tested at least annually?
controls.evidence_type: DR plan, test results, RTO/RPO documentation
common_failures: DR plan not tested (paper exercise only)
RTO not aligned with business needs

controls.title: Contingency Plan — Emergency Mode Operation Plan
controls.description: Establish and implement procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes while operating in emergency mode.
controls.assessment_question: Can critical pharmacy operations (dispensing, billing, inventory) continue during extended IT outage?
controls.evidence_type: Emergency ops procedures, paper workflow SOPs, alternative site agreements

controls.title: Contingency Plan — Testing and Revision Procedures
controls.description: Implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.
controls.assessment_question: Are contingency plans tested and updated at least annually, with documented findings and action items?
controls.evidence_type: Test schedules, test results, revision history
common_failures: Tests are walkthroughs only (no technical restore)

controls.title: Contingency Plan — Applications and Data Criticality Analysis
controls.description: Assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data to support other contingency plan components.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented criticality ranking of ePHI systems supporting RTO/RPO and prioritization?
controls.evidence_type: BIA document, criticality matrix, dependency mapping
common_failures: Dependencies not mapped (e.g., pharmacy system → label printer → network)

controls.title: Evaluation
controls.description: Perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation of security policies and procedures.
controls.assessment_question: Are security policies and controls evaluated at least annually (internal audit, external assessment, or self-assessment)?
controls.evidence_type: Evaluation reports, audit findings, management responses

controls.title: Business Associate Contracts and Other Arrangements
controls.description: A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on its behalf only if satisfactory assurances are obtained.
controls.assessment_question: Are Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) in place with all vendors handling ePHI, including cloud/SaaS providers?
controls.evidence_type: BAA inventory, signed agreements, vendor risk assessments
common_failures: Missing BAAs for SaaS (email, cloud storage, analytics)
BAAs don't reference Security Rule obligations
No vendor security review before engagement

controls.title: Facility Access Controls — Access Control and Validation
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and facilities while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed.
controls.assessment_question: Are facilities with ePHI systems protected by access control (badges, keys, biometrics) with visitor logs?
controls.evidence_type: Access logs, visitor sign-in, badge audit, floor plans

controls.title: Facility Access Controls — Workstation Use Restriction
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures that specify proper use of workstations and restrict access to authorized users.
controls.assessment_question: Are workstations in patient/service areas configured with auto-lock, privacy screens, and restricted to authorized users?
controls.evidence_type: Workstation configuration policy, screen privacy filters, lock timeout settings

controls.title: Facility Access Controls — Facility Security Plan
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and equipment from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a facility security plan covering alarm systems, camera coverage, and environmental controls?
controls.evidence_type: Security plan, alarm test records, camera retention policy

controls.title: Facility Access Controls — Access Control and Validation Records
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility.
controls.assessment_question: Are physical access changes (new locks, door modifications, camera additions) documented and approved?
controls.evidence_type: Change logs, maintenance tickets, approval records
common_failures: No approval workflow for physical changes

controls.title: Facility Access Controls — Maintenance Records
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility related to security.
controls.assessment_question: Are maintenance and repair activities on security systems (locks, cameras, alarms) documented?
controls.evidence_type: Maintenance logs, vendor invoices, work orders

controls.title: Workstation Use
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which they are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation.
controls.assessment_question: Are workstation placement and use policies defined (e.g., no PHI-facing screens in public view, dedicated dispensing terminals)?
controls.evidence_type: Workstation layout diagrams, use policies, privacy filter inventory
common_failures: Dispensing terminals visible to waiting area

controls.title: Workstation Security
controls.description: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information to restrict access to authorized users.
controls.assessment_question: Are all ePHI workstations secured with cable locks, locked cabinets (for laptops), or secured rooms when unattended?
controls.evidence_type: Physical security inventory, cable lock policy, room access logs
common_failures: Laptops left unsecured in patient areas
No cable locks on desktop towers

controls.title: Device and Media Controls — Disposal
controls.description: Implement policies and procedures for the final disposition of electronic media and hardware containing ePHI.
controls.assessment_question: Is ePHI media sanitized (degaussed/destroyed) before disposal or reuse, with certificates of destruction?
controls.evidence_type: Sanitization certificates, disposal logs, vendor contracts

controls.title: Device and Media Controls — Media Re-use
controls.description: Procedures for removal of ePHI from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented sanitization procedure for re-used media (DBAN, secure erase, vendor wiping)?
controls.evidence_type: Sanitization SOP, verification records, tool licenses

controls.title: Device and Media Controls — Accountability
controls.description: Maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media containing ePHI.
controls.assessment_question: Is hardware/media containing ePHI tracked (asset tags, checkout logs, inventory system) when moved?
controls.evidence_type: Asset inventory, transfer logs, chain-of-custody forms
common_failures: No checkout process for backup tapes

controls.title: Device and Media Controls — Data Backup and Storage
controls.description: Create a retrievable, exact copy of ePHI, stored separately from the source, before movement of equipment.
controls.assessment_question: Are backups verified before moving ePHI systems (server migrations, laptop replacements) and stored securely?
controls.evidence_type: Migration playbooks, backup verification, secure storage receipts

controls.title: Access Control — Unique User Identification
controls.description: Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
controls.assessment_question: Does every user have a unique ID (no shared accounts) for all ePHI systems including pharmacy management software?
controls.evidence_type: User account audit, shared account remediation records, IAM policy

controls.title: Access Control — Emergency Access Procedure
controls.description: Establish procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented emergency access procedure (break-glass) with approval, logging, and post-incident review?
controls.evidence_type: Emergency access SOP, break-glass logs, review records

controls.title: Access Control — Automatic Logoff
controls.description: Implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.
controls.assessment_question: Do all ePHI applications and workstations enforce automatic logoff after a defined inactivity period (≤15 min recommended)?
controls.evidence_type: GPO/MDM settings, application configuration, penetration test results
common_failures: No session timeout for remote access

controls.title: Access Control — Encryption and Decryption
controls.description: Implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information.
controls.assessment_question: Is ePHI encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+) on all systems, including backups and removable media?
controls.evidence_type: Encryption policy, certificate inventory, vulnerability scan results

controls.title: Audit Controls
controls.description: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use ePHI.
controls.assessment_question: Are audit logs enabled, protected from tampering, retained per policy (≥6 years), and covering all ePHI access?
controls.evidence_type: Audit configuration, log retention policy, SIEM architecture

controls.title: Integrity — Mechanism to Authenticate ePHI
controls.description: Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
controls.assessment_question: Are integrity controls in place (file hashing, DB checksums, digital signatures) to detect unauthorized modification?
controls.evidence_type: Integrity check logs, hash verification scripts, DB audit triggers
common_failures: No integrity checks on archived data
No detection for ransomware file changes

controls.title: Integrity — Authentication Code
controls.description: Implement electronic signatures or equivalent means to verify ePHI integrity (optional implementation specification).
controls.assessment_question: If used, are electronic signatures or authentication codes implemented per NIST SP 800-63 or equivalent?
controls.evidence_type: Signature policy, certificate authority, validation procedures

controls.title: Person or Entity Authentication
controls.description: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
controls.assessment_question: Is multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforced for all remote access, privileged accounts, and ePHI applications?
controls.evidence_type: MFA enrollment reports, conditional access policies, pen test results

controls.title: Transmission Security — Integrity Controls
controls.description: Implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without detection.
controls.assessment_question: Are message integrity mechanisms (TLS, VPN tunnelling, SFTP instead of FTP) enforced for all ePHI transmission?
controls.evidence_type: Network architecture, protocol inventory, firewall rules
common_failures: FTP instead of SFTP for file transfers
No VPN for remote ePHI access

controls.title: Transmission Security — Encryption
controls.description: Implement a mechanism to encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate.
controls.assessment_question: Is ePHI encrypted during transmission (TLS 1.2+, IPsec VPN, encrypted email gateway) across all channels?
controls.evidence_type: SSL/TLS scan results, VPN config, email gateway policy
